title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's notes for his 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power (p.d.) de Rham complex. The programme appears to be an integral or mod-p analogue of Sullivan's rational de Rham theory of homotopy types. Commutative DG algebras with divided powers stand in for Sullivan's polynomial forms, since the Poincaré lemma holds with divided powers in any characteristic.

Objects on the page:
- k_* is a (simplicial or graded) ground ring with k_0 = k.
- A_* is an augmented object over k_* with degree-zero part A_0 and structure map u_0 : k → A_0.
- Φ_* is a 'standard' system over Z, most plausibly the simplicial divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on the standard simplices. Φ_{*k} = Φ_* ⊗_Z k.
- DRsp(Ss, k_*) appears to be the category of 'special' simplicial DR algebras with divided powers over simplicial sets (Ss) with coefficients k_*.
- T is an extra parameter, perhaps a test object or simplicial set; its meaning is unclear from this page.

Steps on the page:
1. A crossed-out start considers the degree-zero homomorphism k_0 = k → A_0.
2. One obtains a homomorphism A_* → Φ_* ⊗_Z A_0. It sits in a commutative square with k_* ↪ Φ_{*k}, the right vertical map being Φ_* ⊗ u_0.
3. Applying DR(–, T) gives a canonical zig-zag in DRsp(Ss, k_*):
   DR(A^{10}_*, T) → A^{**}_*,
   DR(A^{10}_*, T) → DR(A^{10}_0 ⊗_Z Φ_*, T) ← DR(Φ_{*k}, T),
   plus a diagonal arrow to A^{**}_*. This links a special DR algebra, 'en 3 crans' (in three steps), to the standard DR algebra DR(Φ_{*k}, T). Grothendieck calls the latter 'la plus canonique de toutes'.
4. If A^{**}_* is flasque (resp. a stronger condition, marked 'resp' in the margin), then so is DR(A^{10}_*, T). The diagram then lies in the subcategory DRspeff of 'effective' special DR algebras. Flasque is the analogue of Sullivan's extendability, the Kan-type condition for simplicial algebras of forms.
5. Announced next: categories DRsp'(X,k) and DRspeff'(X,k). They have the same objects but more morphisms, namely '(Witt?) homomorphisms … p.d., respecting J', i.e. divided-power morphisms compatible with the p.d. ideal J, possibly 'generalized' or Witt-type.

Purpose: show that every special (flasque) DR algebra is canonically connected by a short zig-zag to the standard divided-power de Rham algebra. This is a step toward identifying the homotopy categories, i.e. a de Rham theorem / comparison in the p.d. setting.

The neighbouring 'pages' are typescript of SGA 7 Exp. IX (Picard–Lefschetz, Raynaud extension) on the reverse side of reused paper; they are unrelated to this page.
errors: No mathematical error visible. Notation is unexplained on this page (Φ_*, T, A^{10}, A^{**}_*, meaning of 'special' and 'eff'), so correctness of the flasqueness transfer cannot be checked from this page alone.
The final line ('homom de Witt[?] … p.d., respectant J') is heavily corrected and incomplete; the precise morphism notion is not determined here.

ideas.what: Using divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplices (Φ_*) as a characteristic-free replacement for Sullivan's polynomial forms
ideas.modern_name: Integral/p.d. simplicial de Rham algebras (divided-power forms on Δ^n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational case, 1977); H. Cartan 'Théories cohomologiques' (1976); Cenkl–Porter (late 1970s–80s, forms with divided powers / tame homotopy)
ideas.where_published: Only the unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture notes (this cote); some echoes of the homotopy-model ideas in Pursuing Stacks (unsure)

ideas.what: Canonical three-step zig-zag connecting any special flasque DR algebra to the standard DR(Φ_{*k},T), via A_* → Φ_*⊗A_0
ideas.modern_name: Comparison zig-zag of weak equivalences (de Rham theorem for simplicial cdga's)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous comparisons in Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) for the rational case

ideas.what: Flasque (extendable) simplicial DR algebras and stability of flasqueness under DR(–,T)
ideas.modern_name: Extendable simplicial cdga / Kan-type condition (Sullivan, Bousfield–Gugenheim)

ideas.what: Enlarged categories DRsp', DRspeff' with more morphisms: p.d. homomorphisms respecting the divided-power ideal J (possibly 'Witt-type')
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power morphisms of cdga's; possibly related to de Rham–Witt or crystalline-type morphisms

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a hierarchy of categories of 'special' and 'effective' p.d. de Rham algebras over simplicial sets. He then begins enlarging their morphisms to 'Witt'/p.d. homomorphisms respecting J, apparently aiming at a homotopy-theoretic model of homotopy types over Z or F_p by divided-power DR algebras. This 1976 programme predates Mandell's E∞ p-adic models and is largely undocumented.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic algebraic models of homotopy types remain active (Mandell; Toën's affine stacks; derived/animated p.d. algebras; Bhatt–Lurie-type approaches). A Grothendieck attempt with p.d. DR algebras and Witt-type morphisms would be a historically relevant precursor. Its precise content needs the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to a little-known 1976 Grothendieck programme on divided-power de Rham models of homotopy types, which is historically interesting. This particular page, however, contains only a routine comparison zig-zag and the announcement of new morphism categories, without a decisive result.
transcription_corrections: The left-margin note reads 'donnant lieu à un diag. comm.' and goes with the commutative square.
The bottom-left arrow is k_* ↪ Φ_{*k} (an inclusion hook) and the right vertical label is Φ_*⊗_Z u_0; this matches the transcription.
The middle term is DR(A^{10}_0 ⊗_Z Φ_*, T), with subscript 0 on A^{10}; the diagonal arrow goes from DR(Φ_{*k},T) up toward A^{**}_*.
'DR speff' is written as 'DR sp eff' (special effective).
The page number 101 is written at the lower left; the bottom lines are partly obscured and crossed out ('identiques' struck).
